To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ceramide induces growth arrest, c-myc transcription downregulation and pRb underphosphorilation, and that these events are related, and dependent on p21WAF induction, Rb dephosphorilation and E2F binding to Rb.
ceramide induces growth arrest and c-myc down regulation by a pRb-dependent mechanism that is mediated by the p21 induction and E2F inactivation.

ceramide inhibits the transcriptional activity, and therefore the expression, of c-myc, through the downregulation of pRb, which in turn leads to sequestration of E2F and transcriptional inhibition of c-myc.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which the ceramide-induced growth arrest is mediated.
the mechanism of growth inhibition and c-myc down-regulation induced by ceramide.
the mechanism by which cell cycle arrest and c-myc down-regulation are induced by ceramide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ceramide-induced p21 induction is the first step in the process leading to the inhibition of the G1-S transition, the underphosphorylated pRb protein is a key factor in this process, and finally the E2F protein is sequestered into a transcriptionally inert complex with pRb.

ceramide induces growth arrest by inducing the expression of p21 and downregulating the transcription of c-myc through a pathway dependent on p21 expression, pRb underphosphorlation and E2-F sequestering.
ceramide induces cell cycle arrest by a pRb-dependent mechanism and that the pRb-dependent pathway is also involved in the ceramide-induced c-Myc transcription downregulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the growth arrest induced by ceramide is related to the induction of p21, which inhibits CDK activity, leading to the underphosphorylated state of the Rb protein.

ceramide induces cell-cycle arrest by inducing p21WAF, which leads to dephosphorylated pRb, which in turn sequesters E2F, which leads to the downregulation of genes that are required for cell-cycle progression.

ceramide is capable of inducing growth arrest through a mechanism dependent on p21WAF induction and Rb dephosphorilation and that this process is associated with the inhibition of E2F transcriptional activity and c-myc transcription.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ceramide-mediated growth inhibition and the downregulation of cell cycle regulated genes, such as c-myc, are related events, which are mediated by the p21/pRb/EZF pathway.
ceramide-induced c‑myc downregulation is a consequence of the inhibition of E2F transcriptional activity by pRb de-phosphorylation.
ceramide, a key intracellular lipid mediator, is capable of inhibiting cell cycle progression by modulating the activity of a key transcriptional regulatory protein.
